# NaN hold pose: Octave vs the Python port

Input: the grid manager after 10 ticks with Takeoff/Land low, then 150 ticks with the pad confirmed, tracking, the pad at pixel (400, 330) and a hold pose of NaN in all four elements (what the confirmation block captures from a non-finite measured pose). Both columns are the grid manager's `desiredPose` output: Octave runs the chart code extracted from the model (`tools/octave/parity_driver.m`), Python runs `logic/grid_manager.py`, on the same rows ([`tools/evidence.py`](../../tools/evidence.py) `nan-hold`).

| tick | centring | Octave desiredPose (x, y, z, yaw) | Python desiredPose (x, y, z, yaw) | distance from first centring pose (m) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | 1 | (-1.2, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-1.2, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.0000 |
| 12 | 1 | (-1.195646826, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-1.195646826, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.0044 |
| 13 | 1 | (-1.191293652, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-1.191293652, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.0087 |
| 14 | 1 | (-1.186940478, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-1.186940478, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.0131 |
| 60 | 1 | (-0.9866944668, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-0.9866944668, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.2133 |
| 160 | 1 | (-0.5513770521, -1, 0.7, NaN) | (-0.5513770521, -1, 0.7, NaN) | 0.6486 |

Max |Octave - Python| over all 160 ticks and all outputs: 0 (NaN = NaN). GNU Octave, version 9.4.0.

The first centring tick commands the flight-area corner (-1.2, -1.0, 0.7) with a NaN yaw (MATLAB `min(max(NaN, lo), hi)` gives `lo`), and the pose then walks towards the pad (4.35 mm per tick here, under the 5 mm step limit) past 0.5 m from where it started: the model's own 0.5 m displacement limit never fires because its centring origin is NaN.

Pinned by: the committed Octave fixture `tests/fixtures/parity/grid/det_centring_edges` (rows 356-360, NaN hold xy) through `tests/test_parity.py::test_block_matches_octave`; the port's response (pose guard keeps NaN out, output gate refuses the NaN yaw and the 0.5 m entry jump and keeps a finite 0.5 m limit) by `tests/test_safety.py::test_nan_hold_corner_jump_refused_and_limit_kept`; this table by `tools/evidence.py nan-hold --check` in the Octave CI job.
